\paragraph{RE: routing failure.}

tool_args.new_string:
\paragraph{RE: routing failure.}
Oracle routing recovers accuracy (0.802 vs.\ 0.504 single-pass; Table~\ref{tab:batch_composition}), but confusability-aware grouping yields only +1.4\,pp over random ($p \approx 0.19$, n.s.). All practical routing strategies fall below the single-pass baseline (Appendix~\ref{sec:appendix_routing}). The bottleneck is not partitioning quality but routing accuracy: the router must assign each instance to the correct sub-schema without knowing the gold type, and errors cascade into false negatives for the correct batch and false positives for the wrong one. This suggests that routing-aware decomposition---where the decomposition is jointly optimized with a trained router---is a more promising path than post-hoc partitioning of fixed schemas.

tool_args.old_string: For NER, reducing candidate types per prompt is the primary lever. For RE, BCS is a pre-hoc diagnostic: high type-pair similarity (SCS${}\,>\,0.85$) flags degradation without runs, and 22--58\% explained variance means BCS anticipates roughly half of cross-schema variation at zero annotation cost. Na\"{i}ve decompose-then-merge fails (\S\ref{sec:sdgd}), but oracle routing recovers substantial accuracy (72.4\% vs.\ 50.4\%), motivating routing-aware decomposition. In sum, extraction degrades along two separable dimensions---count-driven recall decline and confusability-driven type substitution---replicated across four RE models; NER null on three (8B--70B).
tool_args.new_string:
For NER, reducing candidate types per prompt is the primary lever; the count curve (\S\ref{sec:count_curves}) provides a lookup for expected recall at each schema size.
For RE, BCS enables a pre-hoc diagnostic workflow: (1)~compute pairwise SCS for all type pairs; (2)~flag pairs with SCS${}\,>\,0.85$ as high-risk; (3)~estimate expected accuracy loss from BCS via the regression ($R^2 = 0.22\text{--}0.58$). This anticipates roughly half of cross-schema performance variation at zero annotation cost.

Na\"{i}ve decompose-then-merge fails (\S\ref{sec:sdgd}), but oracle routing recovers substantial accuracy (72.4\% vs.\ 50.4\%), motivating routing-aware decomposition as a path forward. Future work should explore hierarchical extraction (coarse-to-fine type resolution), task-adaptive BCS thresholds calibrated per model family, and joint router-decomposition optimization.

In sum, extraction degrades along two separable dimensions---count-driven recall decline and confusability-driven type substitution---replicated across four RE models; NER null on three (8B--70B).
